findings.reason: The protected solution is already the conventional output-sensitive DFS: extend one immutable root prefix at each node, emit only at leaves, and visit each child once. Its local `TreeNode` model, concept names, and concise traversal are expert interview-quality, so no candidate is justified.

The app-local and immutable Accepted native sources have identical prefix construction, leaf condition, left-before-right traversal, output collection, and return behavior. The app additionally defines the required local `TreeNode` equivalent, while LeetCode injects that model for the native class method.

The former 255-node tier exceeded the 100-node source maximum and used values above 100. Legal 7/31/100-node complete trees now preserve unordered path comparison and bounded values. The current source passes at +0.01 relative exponent with a 0.96x largest runtime ratio; a correct separate root search for every leaf passes every output and fails only scaling at +0.98 with a 20.94x ratio.

The Approach proves that every leaf is reached and emitted exactly once, accurately separates traversal from returned-string cost, labels singleton and value-format boundaries, and no longer presents an empty tree as source-legal.

The hash-bound public Reference remains verified against the source structure, preserving both factual examples, both constraints, and the source image's root-to-leaf relationships through an independently authored local diagram.
